Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes): 
  - Acute 3-day history of profuse watery diarrhoea occurring about hourly while awake. Intermittent crampy lower/central abdominal pain, pain severity ~6/10 when present. Nausea with at least one vomiting episode after milk. Subjective fever/hot sensation. Reports decreased urinary frequency and feeling fluids pass rapidly through. Clinician impression: gastroenteritis. No chronic conditions recalled by patient.
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes): 
  - Father with stage 3 colon cancer (patient unsure of full details).
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines: 
  - Paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Recommended oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) OTC (advice only).
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus): 
  - Not recorded.
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks: 
  - Not recorded.
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use: 
  - Lives with mother and sister; works in an office (government). Reports social smoking (occasional, e.g., weekends) and alcohol use described as occasional heavier drinking 1–2 times/month. Patient reports usually buys own food and does not typically eat with family. No illicit substance use recorded.
- Hearing and vision concerns: 
  - Not recorded.
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm): 
  - Reports some sleep disturbance ("not sleeping" noted). No formal mental health screening documented. No suicidal ideation or self-harm risk described.
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors: 
  - Lives with mother and sister; brother does not live with him. States he prefers to continue working and dislikes taking time off. Has not discussed symptoms in detail with family.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key clinical findings and reasoning:
  - Acute onset (3 days) of profuse watery diarrhoea with frequent stools (~hourly while awake), intermittent crampy central/lower abdominal pain, nausea and at least one vomiting episode after milk, subjective fever, and reduced urinary frequency suggesting risk of dehydration. Household contact (brother) had a similar self-limited diarrhoeal illness.
  - Clinician impression during consult: gastroenteritis, likely self-limited.
  - DDx supports acute viral gastroenteritis as the leading diagnosis; bacterial gastroenteritis and transient lactose intolerance are plausible alternatives or contributors.
- Relevant differentials from DDx that refine the impression:
  - Acute viral gastroenteritis (High likelihood) — consistent with acute profuse watery diarrhoea, cramping, nausea/vomiting, subjective fever, and household contact.
  - Bacterial foodborne gastroenteritis (Medium likelihood) — possible if shared exposure; may cause similar symptoms.
  - Secondary (post-infectious) lactose intolerance (Medium likelihood) — compatible with vomiting after milk and may exacerbate diarrhoea following enteric infection.
- Working diagnosis:
  - Acute gastroenteritis, most likely viral in origin (working diagnosis supported by clinician impression and DDx).
- Management provided / plan:
  - Advice: maintain hydration with clear fluids; use oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) available OTC. Start soft diet as tolerated (soup, mashed foods) and advance gradually.
  - Symptomatic analgesia/antipyretic: paracetamol acceptable (patient already using PRN; dose not documented).
  - Advise avoidance of alcohol while unwell.
  - Safety netting: return or contact clinician if symptoms not settling within 48 hours or if signs of dehydration/worsening occur (further investigations and management may be required).
  - No investigations, prescriptions, or referrals were ordered during this telehealth consult.
- Conflict noted:
  - None between transcript and DDx content.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Acute viral gastroenteritis (e.g., norovirus) — High likelihood.
  - Justification: Acute 3-day course of frequent watery diarrhoea, crampy abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting, subjective fever and a household contact with a similar self-limited illness strongly support a viral etiology.
- Bacterial foodborne gastroenteritis (e.g., ETEC, Salmonella, Campylobacter) — Medium likelihood.
  - Justification: Profuse diarrhoea with cramping and subjective fever could be bacterial if there was a shared contaminated exposure; lacks bloody stools or severe systemic features in history.
- Secondary (post-infectious) lactose intolerance — Medium likelihood.
  - Justification: Vomiting and worsened symptoms after milk intake could reflect transient lactase deficiency following enteric infection and may contribute to persisting loose stools.

  - No immunization review documented.
  - No laboratory investigations (bloods, renal function, electrolytes, stool studies) despite dehydration risk.
  - No formal mental health screening documented.

- Transcript quality notes:
